notes:
The 1944 original, in force 1 January 1944 to 25 February 1956. Words С. В. Михалков and Г. Эль-Регистан, music А. В. Александров.
Included here on the reading that Article 1259 of the Russian Civil Code excludes state symbols from copyright, and that the Russian Federation as successor state carries that exemption to the Soviet anthem - the melody being the same one the Russian anthem uses today. Worth knowing what this rests on: Михалков died in 2009, so on the ordinary life-plus-70 rule the text would run to 2079, and the state-symbol argument is what displaces that.
This version differs from the 1977 revision in more than the Stalin line: each of its three refrains has a different second line (Дружбы / Счастья / Славы), the refrain closes on Знамя советское rather than Партия Ленина, and the third verse is a different text about the army. Russian transcribed from the 1944 text.
Both translations were written for this archive, so no third-party translator's rights attach to them.
ru.translit.txt was generated for this archive, not taken from a published romanization. It follows the scheme already used elsewhere here - ё yo, я ya, ю yu, ж zh, ш sh, щ shch, х kh, ц ts, ы y, ь an apostrophe, and е as ye after a vowel or word-initially. Worth a read before you rely on it.
